belief: Because of my background, I'll always be an outsider.
origins: Accent, skin color, immigration history, religion, or a different way of speaking or eating can set us apart. Repeated questions like “Where are you really from?” or being left out of social circles reinforce a sense of not belonging. We may start to pull back before others can exclude us.
teaches: Paul writes, “There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus,” and “You are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household.” John saw “a multitude too large to count, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne.” Ruth, a foreigner, said, “Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God,” and was welcomed into Israel’s story. In Christ, background becomes a gift in a family that includes every nation, not a barrier.
self_statements: I will never fully belong here.
They will always see me as different.
I have to hide where I am from.
Others have a place and I do not.
errors: Feeling excluded and concluding that I always will be.
questions: When have I felt welcomed, even for a moment?
What would belonging, not sameness, look like for me?
What do I bring from my background that enriches others?
What does Scripture say about every nation worshiping together?
Where might I find communities that welcome people from many backgrounds?
What is one step toward connection?
truth: In Christ I belong to a family that includes every nation and tongue. My background is part of who I am, not a reason to be excluded. I can seek welcoming communities and share what I bring.
hw_truths: I am a fellow citizen and member of God’s household.
There is one family in Christ.
Every nation will stand before the throne.
God settles the lonely in families.
I can seek and build belonging.
log: Each week, note one welcome you received or offered.
actions: Write when you felt excluded and when you felt welcome.
Tell someone about your culture or background.
Visit a church or group with diverse members.
prayer: Lord, You gather people from every nation. Make me at home in Your family, heal the sting of being excluded, and let me welcome others. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am a fellow citizen and a member of God’s household.”
